I've gone into this beta (on PS4) with admittedly *very* low expectations, for several reasons:

* 1 I do not like Gearbox as a developer much.

* 2 I don't like MOBAs.

So it would seem that I've been doomed to not enjoy this game from the get-go. But since it was an open beta, I gave it a shot anyway. And I surprisingly ended up enjoying my time with it (Expectations being incredibly low though they were), but I do have a *lot* of thoughts about it.

__________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________

**The Positive**

The gameplay is fairly addicting. Since it's designed after a MOBA, one of its biggest strengths is the huge cast of characters, build options, and loadouts available. There's a large amount of things to go through. And most matches tend to go on for a fairly lengthy amount of time, thus giving you a lot of time to become versed with how your character operates. And there's a lot of different gameplay styles - From the ranged tanky sorts, to close-ranged melee glass cannons, and healers/buffers to support your team.

I've sunken more hours than I expected into the beta, and there's *still* a lot more to go through. So I'm impressed with the game enough so far. But of course, there's a lot of other things that are not so positive....

___________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________

**Everything else**

It being a Gearbox game sadly is stuck with a lot of problems I had with Borderlands. Beyond the nausea inducing "humor". It possesses a familiar clunkiness with collision, except probably even worse due to the fact that this is a competitive Multiplayer game.

* Clunkiness

This extends into pretty much every aspect of the gameplay. You'll get stuck on everything in sight. Every corner that slightly juts out from the rest of the wall, every gentle incline on the ground. You'll constantly run into *something* that brings you to a dead stop, and if you are playing one of the massive Tank characters, good fucking luck. Jumping has similar problems to Borderlands, in that it's too floaty for a lot of characters, and if you collide with something during a jump, you'll probably be floating in the air for another 2 or 3 seconds before you hit the ground. This happening while surrounded by enemies and minions drives me insane. And speaking of minions...

* You can collide into minions.

Think about that for a moment. If you are playing a massive character like [Montana](http://www.allthatsepic.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/09/battleborn-montana.jpg), and you end up surrounded by minions. You literally cannot move in any direction. Now some might say this is a reasonable punishment for getting in the middle of minions, but there are other minions who are just as massive as you are, who will run into you from behind and shove you into walls, into enemies, in between them, and get you completely stuck. Honestly, I think this is an atrocious problem that shouldn't be happening, and is tied with the mobility issues in the game.

* 1st person + tiny FOV

I honestly don't think the game should be 100% first person. For some characters it might make sense, but for other characters, specifically melee characters, this can cause you to get completely lost in the action.

The best way I can describe it, is like playing Diablo 3 in first person. Imagine playing something like [this](http://www.diabloii.net/wp-content/uploads/2012/03/p14-tomb-guardians.jpg), entirely in first person, with a melee character. It would drive you insane.

* Visual clutter.

Extending from my point about Diablo 3, there's way too much visual vomit all over the screen. Spell effects and explosions overlap each other and become an indiscernible mess. Did that giant purple explosion come from our team or theirs? Well I'm not dead, so I guess I have my answer. There's shit all over the place at all times, and all this visual mess leads me to my next point...

* Framerate issues

The game being at 30fps is questionable enough as it is. But there were a lot of times in the action where framerate tanks below 30, sometimes down to 20. I know beta is beta, and this is something that could get ironed out. But my grievances towards Gearbox make me feel that they won't care to fix it. While I don't really want to make this comparison - That *other* game by Blizzard is going to run on 60fps for consoles.

________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________

**Conclusion**

While I do give props to Gearbox for making a game format I loathe into something I enjoy, they're not the first game to do that (That would be Monday Night Combat, which I found to be more enjoyable), they still produced something I found some enjoyment in. The game has enough addicting elements to it for me to sink hours into, but there's way too many problems with clunkiness and questionable design choices that make me worry I would truly enjoy it. In the end, I think I'll hold off on it.
